bullets.text: ML is a subfield of AI, building systems that learn from data without explicit programming.
Core idea: systems learn patterns and make decisions with minimal human intervention.
Crucial in modern technology: image recognition, NLP, predictive analytics, autonomous vehicles.
Recent growth due to large datasets, improved computational power, and advanced algorithms.
Broadly classified into Supervised, Unsupervised, and Reinforcement Learning.
Supervised Learning: Model trained on labeled data to predict known outputs (e.g., Regression, Classification).
Unsupervised Learning: Model trained on unlabeled data to find hidden patterns (e.g., Clustering, Dimensionality Reduction).
Reinforcement Learning: Agent learns by interacting with an environment to maximize cumulative rewards.
Model Training: Feeding data to a model to learn patterns and adjust internal parameters.
Features and Labels: Input variables (features) and target outputs (labels) in supervised learning.
Training and Testing Sets: Data divided to train the model and evaluate its performance on unseen data.
Overfitting: Model learns training data too well, including noise, leading to poor generalization.
Underfitting: Model is too simple and fails to capture important patterns in the data.
Linear Regression: Models linear relationships for regression tasks.
Logistic Regression: Used for classification, predicts probability of class membership.
Decision Trees: Non-linear model splitting data based on feature values, easy to interpret.
Random Forest: Ensemble method combining multiple decision trees for improved performance.
Support Vector Machines (SVM): Finds optimal hyperplane to separate different classes.
Neural Networks: Brain-inspired, learns complex patterns, widely used in deep learning.
Healthcare: Disease diagnosis, drug discovery, personalized treatment recommendations.
Finance: Fraud detection, credit scoring, algorithmic trading.
Marketing: Customer segmentation, personalized recommendations, targeted advertising.
Autonomous Vehicles: Processing sensor data, decision-making, safe navigation.
Natural Language Processing (NLP): Language translation, sentiment analysis, text summarization.
Training and Testing: Evaluate model performance using separate datasets with metrics like accuracy or MSE.
Cross-Validation: Technique to ensure model generalizes well by splitting data into multiple subsets.
Hyperparameter Tuning: Optimizing model settings (hyperparameters) for optimal performance.
Data Quality and Quantity: Requires large amounts of accurate, consistent, and complete data.
Interpretability: Many complex models are difficult to understand, problematic in high-stakes applications.
Bias in Data: Models can inherit biases from training data, leading to unfair outcomes.
Overfitting and Underfitting: Common issues affecting a model's ability to generalize.
Continuous evolution with advancements in deep learning, reinforcement learning, and explainable AI (XAI).
Increased computational power and datasets will expand ML's role across industries.
Greater integration into daily life, enabling smarter technologies.
Ethical considerations and responsible AI practices will be essential.
